policyTitle: Travel and Subsistence Policy and Employee Guidance
issuingTrust: NHS Trust (issuer not explicitly named in document)
excessMileageRule: Home to base return mileage must be deducted from total miles travelled. Calculated as: (Home to base return) × 2, then subtract from total miles travelled for work purposes. Only excess miles beyond the home-to-base return journey are claimable.

accommodationEligibility.rule: Distance from home address to training venue must be in excess of 1 hour (as determined by AA route planner or HERE Maps) AND event must be more than 1 day in duration. Accommodation not normally provided for 1-day events. Accommodation not normally provided prior to course start date, except where courses have early commencement time and travel time would exceed 1 hour.
Distance from home address to venue must be more than 1 hour (as determined by AA route planner or HERE Maps) AND event must be more than 1 day in duration.

approvalRules.expenseType: general travel and subsistence (not part of standard duties)
approvalRules.approver: Line manager with authorised signatory approval for expenses

bookingProcess.bookingSystem: Redfern travel booking system via admin team

exceptions.condition: Employee is on long-term sick leave
Accommodation has been offered and turned down, unless good reason can be shown (e.g., carer responsibilities)
Course has early commencement time and travel time would be in excess of 1 hour
Urgent requirement exists for employee to book public transport or accommodation themselves rather than through Trust booking system

prohibitions.rule: Claims must not be authorised by colleagues or by those without authorised signatory approval
Where meals are included in accommodation booking, employees will not be permitted to claim any other subsistence in relation to meals
Falsely claiming travel and other expenses to which employees are not entitled is fraudulent and will result in criminal and/or disciplinary action
Employees must not undertake business journeys without appropriate business cover in vehicle insurance; failure to do so may invalidate the policy
Travel time will not be payable if employee is asked to work from an alternative base station for their full shift; employee must travel to alternative location in their own time

evidenceRequirements.expenseType: meals and subsistence (not included in accommodation)

evidenceRequirements.requirement: Employee declaration stating claim is accurate, legitimate and incurred in course of duties
Line manager must annually verify: valid driving licence, Certificate of Motor Insurance policy document (with class 1 business cover), MOT Test Certificate, Road Fund Tax
Employee must hold appropriate and valid driving licence for their class of vehicle; vehicle must be roadworthy with valid insurance and MOT certificates

unhandled.topic: travel time reconciliation and payment conditions
unhandled.rawText: Section 11 describes complex reconciliation rules for travel time where employees are stood down from normal shifts to attend training. Hours that would have been worked on normal shifts are reconciled against excess travel time claims. Staff will only be able to claim travel time in excess of hours reconciled. Overtime may be claimed for hours worked in excess, except for relief staff where hours are reconciled through Scheduling Team.

Section 3.7 states: 'If employees are required to attend training, then the principle of a day for a day will be applied. Arrangements for travel time are as detailed in the employee guidance that should be read in conjunction with this policy.' This principle is referenced but detailed implementation is in employee guidance.

Section 3.4: 'To support the environment and Green agenda, prior to undertaking journeys, employees should consider, whether their journeys are necessary i.e. can the duties be performed satisfactorily virtually or by telephone, rather than in person. Undertaking the duties via a virtual meeting should always be considered first.'
Section 6.1 change log notes: 'Change of basis of calculation from shortest to quickest' (February 2022). Policy now specifies 'quickest route' for journey planning.

Employee Guidance Section 3 states: 'Expenses are paid a month in arrears provided the claim is submitted by the 5th of the following month. For example, expenses incurred in September would be paid into your October salary.'
